title: She didn’t silence a man.
paragraphs: She tried to silence a mirror.
Because when truth speaks, it doesn’t just echo in the air…
It exposes what we’ve been hiding in the dark.
And Herodias could not bear what she saw.
It was conviction… twisted into revenge.
John the Baptist didn’t attack her.
He didn’t rally a mob against her.
“It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.” (Mark 6:18)
Here’s the tension we don’t like to admit:
Sometimes the voice we hate the most…
Is the one telling us the truth we refuse to face.
“So Herodias nursed a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she was not able to.”
And here’s where it gets dangerous.
Because unrepented sin doesn’t stay quiet.
Then silencing anything—or anyone—that threatens it.
Even if it means killing the truth.
And suddenly, a prophet’s life became the price of protecting a sinful relationship.
“So he immediately sent an executioner with orders to bring John’s head.”
Because even in death, John’s life screamed the cost of truth…
And the danger of hardened hearts.
Who are you in this story?
Not who you want to be.
Speaking truth even when it costs you everything?
Resenting the very voice God sent to wake you up?
We hate being confronted about it.
We reject the way He exposes what we love more than Him.
“For everyone who does evil hates the light and will not come into the light for fear that their deeds will be exposed.” (John 3:20)
Because this story doesn’t end with John.
But he could not remove it.
But he could not cleanse them.
But he could not provide redemption.
Jesus didn’t come to silence sinners.
Not to expose you and leave you in shame.
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Not after you cleaned your life.
While you were still in it.
That’s the difference between Herodias and the redeemed.
You don’t have to kill the voice convicting you.
You don’t have to silence truth.
Because the same truth that exposes you…
Is the same truth that can free you.
“Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.” (John 8:32)
But only if you stop running.
There might be something in your life you’re protecting.
And every time truth gets close…
Don’t let pride turn conviction into hatred.
Don’t let sin convince you that truth is the problem.
Jesus is not waiting to condemn you.
There is more grace in Christ…
Than there is sin in you.
